full_judgment: 2. In Administrative Tribunal Case No. 190 of 1989, the petitioner Md. Abdus Salam's case is that he was appointed Economic Investigator of the Bangladesh National Wages and Productivity Commission in 1982. In all other Administrative Tribunal cases the cases of the petitioners are that they were appointed in the Bangladesh Jatiya Mohila Sangstha on various dates and served under the Bangladesh Jatiya Mohila Sangstha in different districts. All the petitioners were retrenched while serving in their respective posts due to administrative re-organization in 1982. Thereafter they obtained nominations for absorption under the Surplus Public Servants Absorption Ordinance, 1985. According to the petitioners while they were serving as such one anonymous letter was received by respondent No. 1 on 22.11.86 containing certain allegations against them. On the basis of those allegations respondent No. 1 placed the petitioners under suspension. Charges were drawn against the petitioners which were denied by all the petitioners by submitting written statements. The petitioners were neither given a personal hearing nor served with a second show cause notice. Thereafter respondent No. 1 illegally removed the petitioners from services and directed them to refund the money they had received on account of salaries and allowances. The authority also failed to take final decision within the statutory period of limitation of 150 days. The petitioners preferred appeals to the relevant authorities and those were rejected. Thereafter the petitioners filed the cases for a declaration that their appointments/nominations are valid and the orders of removal from services are Illegal and void and also for a declaration that they are still in service.
